column3: Close to the Aramaic.

“Ministers” is rendered “treasurers,” and “authorities” “rulers.”
“With power” is rendered “loudly”; “to you [they are] saying” is rendered “To you the command is given,” and “languages” “men of every language.”
“Zither” is rendered “lyre,” “harp” “psaltery,” and “pipe” “bagpipe”; “pay homage” is rendered “worship.”
“At that moment” is rendered “immediately”; “pay homage” is rendered “worship.”
The Aramaic here lacks the sixth instrument (“pipe”), which NASB includes (“bagpipe”); “languages” is rendered “men of every language.”
“Ate their pieces” (an idiom) is rendered “brought charges against.”
Close to the Aramaic.
Instrument names are rendered as in verse 5; “pay homage” is rendered “worship.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“Have not set discretion to you” is rendered “have disregarded you,” “pay reverence” “serve,” and “pay homage” “worship.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“Purpose?” is rendered “Is it true … ?”
NASB supplies “very well” for the unfinished condition; “at that moment” is rendered “immediately.”
“To send back to you” is rendered “to give you an answer”; NASB places “O Nebuchadnezzar” in the address, while the Aramaic reads “to the king, Nebuchadnezzar.”
“If there is our God” is rendered “If it be so, our God”; the meaning is uncertain.
NASB supplies “He does” in “even if He does not.”
“The image of his face was changed” is rendered “his facial expression was altered”; “one seven” is rendered “seven times.”
“Mighty men of power” is rendered “valiant warriors.”
The garment words are uncertain; NASB renders them “trousers,” “coats,” “caps,” and “other clothes,” in a different order.
“Harsh” is rendered “urgent.”
NASB adds “still.”
“Counselors” is rendered “high officials.”
Close to the Aramaic.
Close to the Aramaic.
“Mantles” is rendered “trousers,” and “changed” “damaged.”
“Violated the word of the king” is rendered “violating the king’s command”; “gave their body” is rendered “yielded up their bodies.”
“Negligence” is rendered “anything offensive,” and “made members” “torn limb from limb.”
Close to the Aramaic.
